 THIS MFA IS FILED U/S 173(1) OF MV ACT AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 19.05.2021 PASSED IN MVC NO.921/2017 ON THE FILE OF THE III ADDITIONAL SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE AND MEMBER, MACT, MANGALURU D.K, PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION  THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE DR. JUSTICE CHILLAKUR SUMALATHA  ORAL JUDGMENT Heard Sri. Ravishankar Shastry G, learned counsel for the appellant as well as Sri.Ravishankar C.R,
learned counsel for respondent No.2-Insurnace Company.
2.
This is a claimant's appeal.

The claimant challenges the award that is passed by the Motor NC:
2024:KHC:37138 Accidents Claims Tribunal, Mangaluru in M.V.C. No.921/2017 dated 19.05.2021.
3.
On the ground that he sustained grievous injuries due to the accident and became permanently disabled, the appellant filed a petition claiming compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- in total.
The tribunal through the impugned order awarded a sum of Rs.2,89,182/- as compensation.
Dissatisfied with the same, the claimant is before this Court.
4. Arguing the matter, Sri.Ravishankar Shastry.
G learned counsel for appellant submits that the appellant sustained grievous injuries in a road traffic accident and took treatment as inpatient for a period of 21 days.
However, his right upper limb was paralyzed and he is unable to do anything with his right arm.
Though, through the evidence of PW-2 it is clearly established that the permanent disability is 35%, the tribunal assessed and took the percentage of disability as 11% which is unjustifiable.
Learned counsel further submits that the appellant was earning Rs.10,500/- per month by the date of accident by working as Office Assistant at Kanchana Udyog, Mangalore.

sentences.text: However, deducting the contribution of the appellant to ESI and PF, the tribunal took the income as Rs.9,056/-per month which is unjustifiable.

Learned counsel submits that on one hand the tribunal failed to award the medical expenses incurred on the ground that the same was reimbursed by the ESI but on the otherhand failed to take the gross salary of the appellant which is unjustifiable.

6. Learned counsel further submits that the amount awarded as compensation by the tribunal under all heads is grossly low and therefore a justifiable sum is required to be awarded as compensation.
7.

Sri .Ravishankar C.R, learned counsel for respondent No.2 though contends that the compensation awarded by the tribunal is justifiable, learned counsel did NC: 2024:KHC:37138 not deny the submission that the gross salary of Rs.10,500/- is required to be taken to compute the compensation which the appellant is entitled under the head loss of future earnings due to permanent physical disability.

8. As per the contents of Ex.P-7 Wound Certificate, the appellant sustained abrasion on right side of forehead, fracture of C-6 and C-7 vertebra, post traumatic neuropraxic injury and joint dislocation of right arm.
The disability certificate issued by PW-2 which is marked as Ex.P-16 reveals that he observed complete paralyses of right arm.
There were no moments of right elbow and shoulder joint.
PW-2 assessed the permanent disability in respect of right upper limb as 35%.
9. Discussing the merits of the matter, the tribunal took the disability as 11%.

However, having considered the fact that the appellant is not in a position to move the right upper limb which is a prime organ for a human to attend his daily pursuits as well as the office duties, this NC:
2024:KHC:37138 Court is of the view that the disability in respect of whole body is required to be taken as 15%.

As earlier indicated, the salary of the appellant as established by him is Rs.10,500/-
per month.
10. There is no denial of the fact that the appellant was aged about 36 years by the date of accident.

Thus, as per the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Company Limited vs.
Pranay Sethi and Others reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 case

Also the multiplier applicable as per the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Sarla Verma and Others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and Another reported in 2009 SAR (Civ) is '15'.
11.

Thus, the compensation which the appellant is entitled under the head loss of future earnings due to permanent physical disability is as under:-
 Heads Amount in Rs.

3 Add 40% towards future 1,76,400-00 prospects Apply appropriate multiplier 26,46,000-00 '15'
Loss of future earnings, 3,96,900-00 permanent physical disability being 15%
12.
This Court is of the view that the appellant would have not attended his normal pursuits atleast for a period of four months.

Thus, the loss of earnings during laid up period comes to Rs.42,000/-
(Rs.10,500 x 4).
The tribunal failed to award any compensation towards loss of amenities in life.

Having considered the fact that the appellant sustained grievous injury to his right upper limb and the said limb was paralyzed, due to the injury sustained, this Court is of the view that the appellant is entitled to a sum of Rs.50,000/- towards loss of amenities in life.
Also the compensation awarded under the head pain and suffering and for food, attendant, nourishment and conveyance charges requires marginal enhancement.

Thus, the compensation which the appellant is entitled under different heads is as under:
 Heads Amount in Rs.
Compensation for pain and 60,000-00 suffering Medical expenses 50-00 Towards Food, Attendant, 25,000-00 extra nourishment and conveyance charges Loss of income during laid 42,000-00 up period Loss of future earnings 3,96,900-00 Loss of amenities in life 50,000-00  TOTAL 5,73,950-00 14.
Thus, the justifiable sum which the appellant is entitled to as compensation in the light of the injuries sustained by him is Rs.5,73,950/-.

Thus, the appeal is disposed of with the following:-
ORDER i.
The appeal is allowed in part ii.
